how: A member proposes and maps the Wheel before another participant joins the visible first squares.
Participants recruit game-thread readers and script runners to create and defend the Wheel.
A border instruction receives a bare acceptance rather than a reasoned commitment.
Participants choose the Wheel and specify an order for drawing its parts.
Helpers report finding the initial squares and building a shared white line.
Coordinates and templates locate the initial build and guide later repairs.
Members share scripts, correct failures and report running them across servers.
Participants explicitly weigh too few workers against a larger opponent when considering relocation.
Participants make upkeep the priority and repair the Wheel around an advancing stripe.
Participants distinguish faulty or stale scripts and independent projects from the coordinated Wheel.
Participants exchange border terms, request pauses and redirect neighbour negotiations.
Participants cede a corner, incorporate a neighbouring flag and prohibit crossing it with a proposed addition.
A request for Lions helmet help is followed by a completion title without exposing the linked pixel work.
Visitors offer reciprocal help and promise maintenance around the Wheel.
Participants agree to group hockey logos and move official planning to a shared hub.
Participants debate relocation and reject one destination before publishing a script for the relocated logo.
Participants carry border messages and report contacts with other hockey groups.
A Buffalo builder asks for leaders to negotiate and receives a reply naming the negotiating hub.
Participants use a familiar hockey saying to defend script use and recast rivalry as collective hockey identity.
A participant invokes the existing Leafs rivalry in order to suspend it for shared hockey defence.
A maintainer names Bruins and Blues logos in attack talk that another participant discourages.
Fake allegiance and retirement posts invite both enjoyment and objections under the April Fools frame.
Participants direct official canvas planning into a dedicated coalition subreddit.
Participants celebrate completion and thank those who kept the Wheel alive at closure.
Participants mourn the first Wheel and recount a limited victory within its loss.
A participant proposes using the temporary canvas logo as the subreddit sidebar picture.
Participants propose deliberate overwriting and call for defeating a competing drawing.
Participants carry the contest through cheating accusations, entitlement counterclaims and defended overwrites.
A sports tease answers a help request without establishing an attack on the requested canvas work.
A mapped member proposal gives later helpers a concrete location and first squares to join.
Game-thread recruitment is answered by a participant reporting that the script is running.
A recruitment exchange contains an explicit bare acceptance by running the shared script.
The completion announcement immediately turns into an instruction to maintain the finished work.
The same announcement marks the work done and celebrates it collectively.
Participants justify continued scripts as preserving art while supporters sleep or work.
A Leafs representative offers help against the ribbon in return for future assistance.
Border negotiation includes a promise to maintain around the neighbouring Wheel.
The Original 6 invitation explicitly offers joint upkeep as an alternative to fighting alone.
Mobilisation for the Wheel is followed by explicit calls to defeat the Mariners.
A temptation to attack hockey rivals receives a refusal grounded in the risk of retaliation.
Complaints about scripted encroachment prompt a call for leader talks and a reply directing negotiation.
Explicit obstruction and entitlement accusations receive a defence of maintaining the Wheel.
The border dispute elicits a request for leaders and a reply naming a negotiating venue.
Automation also enters through rebuilding after displacement, before a completed mark needs routine upkeep.
Misdirected automation can be stopped in favour of manual reference repairs rather than producing ever more machine placement.
When a shared script fails, continued upkeep depends on returning to reference-led manual fixes.
Relocation restarts construction through a new script, drawing instructions and practical setup help.
Anticipated overlap can initiate border negotiations before a completed mark enters maintenance.
Agreements constrain automated overlap only when active script versions and absent users can be reached or corrected.
Implementing negotiated targets requires reaching stale-script users or making the shared script remotely updatable.
A judgement of insufficient manpower does not produce movement while participants insist on holding the prior spot.
A coalition formed for mutual protection can displace nonmembers and contest their claims to the new area.
This room includes explicit allocation of recruits and official planning, so its coordination cannot be described as wholly undecided.
Requests for leaders establish sought interlocutors, while binding mandate and the reason an agreement failed remain unresolved.
Reported agreement failure does not by itself establish repudiated representative authority when stale scripts also persist.
A completed interim image can prompt reuse in the host subreddit before the final close.
After closure, members can demand moral accountability from their own organisers for preserving the mark by displacing others.
An organiser explicitly justifies displacement by the wish to immortalise the community mark.
A help request and completion title establish an appeal and claimed outcome without proving which room supplied the placements.
A negotiated offer establishes promised assistance but does not establish that all placers performed it.
The initial proposal already includes a template, so these concepts do not expose design argument being resolved by a later template.
Celebration and retrospective labour accounts are visible without establishing that marking the work caused record-making.
The sidebar proposal precedes closure and does not establish that a final record caused the reuse decision.
Dedicated planning and reported stickying do not reveal whether canvas-call volume caused moderator containment or posting restrictions.
A territorial declaration and neighbour objection do not establish effective host authority governing guest artwork.
Post-close criticism judges the original overwrite without documenting a dispute over cleanup or the version preserved in a shared copy.
